title: Nodes persist under extension of algebraically closed fields
statement: Let $k\subseteq\Omega$ be algebraically closed fields [def-weil-algebraic-closure], with $\Omega$ a field extension of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension], and let $C$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume that every point of $C$ at which $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is not smooth (has no open neighbourhood smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]) has maximal-ideal-adic completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] isomorphic as a ring to $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Put $C_\Omega=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then every point of $C_\Omega$ at which $C_\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is not smooth has completed local ring isomorphic as a ring to $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. The scheme $C$ may be empty; no quasi-compactness, separatedness or dimension hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Stacks Tag 0C56 (curves.tex, lemma-node-field-extension), direction (1)$\Rightarrow$(2) for algebraically closed $k\subseteq K$, with Varieties lemma-base-change-complete-local-ring for the completed local rings.

proof.text: Let $y\in C_\Omega$ be nonsmooth and let $x$ be its image in $C$. A smooth open neighbourhood of $x$ would pull back to a smooth open neighbourhood of $y$, by clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. Thus $x$ is nonsmooth and the hypothesis gives $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,x}\cong k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ as rings. By [lem-trf-nodal-completion-rational-point], $x$ is closed and the structure map $k\to\kappa(x)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0C56, lemma-node-field-extension, closed-point reduction; abstract ring-isomorphism refinement extracted to the rational-point node.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}S$ containing $x$, with $S$ finitely generated over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Its prime $\mathfrak p$ is maximal and $S/\mathfrak p=k$ by Step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $U_\Omega=\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_k\Omega)$. The primes over $\mathfrak p$ are those of $(S/\mathfrak p)\otimes_k\Omega=\Omega$, hence there is exactly one: $\mathfrak q=\ker(S\otimes_k\Omega\to\Omega)$, $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\bar s\lambda$. It represents $y$. Set $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$ and $B=(S\otimes_k\Omega)_{\mathfrak q}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], these identify with $\mathcal O_{C,x}$ and $\mathcal O_{C_\Omega,y}$ via the germ maps.

source.place: Tag 0C56, affine scalar-extension argument, and varieties.tex Tag 0C54, lemma-base-change-complete-local-ring.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-rational-nodal-completion-algebra] to $S,\mathfrak p,A$: it replaces the abstract ring isomorphism by a continuous $k$-algebra presentation $k[[u,v]]\twoheadrightarrow\widehat A$ with kernel $(uv)$. Apply the base-change clause of [lem-trf-separable-closed-point-formal-presentation] to this presentation, with $F=S/\mathfrak p=k$, $K=\Omega$, $n=2$, and $f_1=uv$. The residue-field hypothesis is satisfied because $k/k$ is finite separable; the coefficient section is the structure map. That clause applies to every presentation and to exactly the prime $\mathfrak q$ of Step 2. It gives $\widehat B\cong\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ as complete local $\Omega$-algebras, hence as rings, as required.

proof.text: The argument applies to every nonsmooth point $y$ of $C_\Omega$. If $C$ is empty there are no such points and the assertion is vacuous; otherwise the preceding construction is pointwise and imposes no quasi-compactness, separatedness, or dimension hypothesis beyond local finite type.
